answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals account age times honest epochs, so a clone minted today cannot wander far no matter how many fakes exist. An attacker must run thousands of idle identities for months, paying compute and staked collateral, while every fraud epoch zeroes accrued trust and forfeits deposits. Like timber that needs decades before it can bear marble, trust cannot be bought, only grown, making fake identity a slow, negative-return investment instead of a cheap shortcut.
